topic: Before publishing on the Play Store: 5 things to remember

cover.headline: 5 things to check before you publish on the Play Store
cover.subtitle: A pre-launch checklist so your first release doesn't get stuck in review

slides.title: Upload a signed App Bundle
slides.description: New apps on Google Play are published as an Android App Bundle (.aab), signed with your upload key. Play App Signing then signs what users download.
bullets: Back up the upload keystore and its passwords
Never commit the keystore or passwords to Git
slides.tip: Lost your upload key? With Play App Signing you can request a reset, but it takes time. Back it up today.

slides.title: Target the required API level
slides.description: Since Aug 31, 2026, new apps and updates must target Android 16 (API 36). The bar rises every year, so check the current rule before each release.
bullets: Set targetSdk = 36 in your app module
Test on a device or emulator running Android 16
slides.tip: Wear OS, Automotive and TV apps have different targets. Check Play's target API page for yours.

slides.title: Shrink and test the release build

code.explanation: R8 removes unused code and resources. Test the release build itself: shrinking can break libraries that rely on reflection.

slides.title: Complete App content honestly
slides.description: Play Console won't let you publish until the App content section is done, and it must match what your app really does.
bullets: A public, accurate privacy policy URL
Data safety form, including analytics and crash SDKs

slides.title: Test with real users first
slides.description: Personal developer accounts created after Nov 2023 must run a closed test (currently 12 testers for 14 days) before production access.
bullets: Read the pre-launch report for crashes
Fix crashes and ANRs flagged in Android vitals
Check sign-in, payments and deep links on real devices
slides.tip: Requirements change. Confirm yours in Play Console before you plan a launch date.

slides.title: Before you hit Publish
bullets: App content and Data safety complete

slides.title: Ship once, ship clean
slides.description: A calm launch is mostly preparation. Run this checklist on every release, not just the first one.

caption.caption:
Your first Play Store release shouldn't get stuck in review because of something on a checklist.

Here are 5 things to check before you hit Publish: a signed App Bundle, the required target API level, a tested release build, an honest App content section, and a real closed test.

Policies change every year, so confirm the current rules in Play Console before you launch.
caption.cta: Save this for your next release and share it with an Android dev who's about to ship.
